after.text: Let E be any real normed vector space whose additive group is a normed additive commutative group, with a complete norm topology, a second-countable topology, and a measurable structure equal to its Borel structure. Let mu be any Gaussian probability measure on E, in the sense that every continuous real linear functional has a Gaussian pushforward; its mean is unrestricted and degeneracy is allowed. Let L be any nonnegative real Lipschitz constant, including L = 0, and let f: E -> R satisfy the global bound |f(x) - f(y)| <= L ||x - y|| for all x,y in E. Then f is Bochner integrable with respect to mu, and for every real t, including negative t and t = 0, the function x |-> exp(t (f(x) - m)), where m = integral_E f(z) dmu(z) is the actual mean of f under mu, is Bochner integrable with respect to mu. The conclusion is integrability of each such centered exponential; it supplies no quantitative bound on its integral.

after.text: Let E be any complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with a normed additive commutative group structure and its Borel measurable structure, and let S be any measurable space. Zero-dimensional E is allowed, and S has no topological or cardinality restriction. Let V: E -> R be twice continuously Frechet differentiable, and let kappa be a real number with 1 <= kappa. Assume that for every x,v in E, kappa^(-1) ||v||^2 <= D(DV)(x)[v][v] <= ||v||^2, where D(DV)(x)[v][v] denotes the iterated actual real Frechet derivative. Let eta: S -> R and y: S -> E be measurable, and suppose eta(s) > 0 for every s in S. Define F(s,x) = V(x) + (eta(s)^(-1)/2) ||x - y(s)||^2. There exists a measurable p: S -> E such that all of the following hold simultaneously: (1) For every s, p(s) + eta(s) grad V(p(s)) = y(s), using real scalar multiplication and the real Hilbert Riesz gradient. (2) For every s in S and z in E, F(s,p(s)) + ((kappa^(-1) + eta(s)^(-1))/2) ||z - p(s)||^2 <= F(s,z), and [F(s,z) <= F(s,p(s)) if and only if z = p(s)]. (3) For every s,t in S, eta(s) = eta(t) implies ||p(s) - p(t)|| <= ||y(s) - y(t)||. With this same p, define G: S x E -> E by G(s,z) = grad V(p(s) + sqrt(eta(s)) z), using real scalar multiplication. Then G is measurable for the product measurable structure, and for every s,t in S and z,w in E, eta(s) = eta(t) implies ||G(s,z) - G(t,w)|| <= ||y(s) - y(t)|| + sqrt(eta(s)) ||z - w||. Furthermore, there exists a measurable probability kernel K from S to E such that, for every s, K(s) is the literal pushforward of the canonical centered covariance-identity Gaussian measure on E under z |-> G(s,z). For every s, the identity function u |-> u is Bochner integrable under K(s); and for every a in E and every real r, the function u |-> exp(r <a, u - m_s>), where m_s = integral_E v dK(s)(v) is the actual mean of this same output law, is Bochner integrable under K(s). The quantification includes a = 0 and all signs of r. No quantitative exponential-moment bound, equality of m_s to a separately specified gradient, sampling algorithm, or runtime guarantee is asserted.
